scope: Atomic compare-and-swap for account-private manual media labels
implemented: Additive SQLite 122 and PostgreSQL 024 migrations add an opaque version column. Existing records retain their labels and receive the legacy migration token; every subsequent successful write rotates a cryptographically random 128-bit token.

Public PUT/DELETE bodies require expected_version. Empty string means observed absence. Atomic insert-if-absent, version-matching update and version-matching deletion reject stale state with HTTP 409 / CONFLICT. Internal repository compatibility calls may omit the comparison; HTTP callers cannot.

GET returns the current version. The client validates and sends the observed version, never retries a conflicting write automatically, and requires explicit reload/reselection. Drafts affected by another session's invalidation display a conflict instead of silently disappearing.

Socket invalidations while a version-checked write is pending revoke visible media but allow the atomic write receipt to finish. This handles an originating session's own socket echo arriving before its HTTP response. Successful writes then reload canonical state.
OpenAPI documents required expected versions, returned opaque versions and conflict responses. No media plaintext or URLs were added to the server payload.

verification.detail: Eight competing creates and eight competing updates each accept exactly one caller; stale delete, delete/recreate ABA, expected-absence delete, token rotation, malformed versions and missing HTTP expected_version are covered.
